notice: This 0-5 answer scale is the product's approved estimation convention. It is not a universal industry standard.

dimensions.question: How much business functionality is being built or changed?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No business functionality is being added or changed in this work.
levels.example: A purely technical or infrastructure change with no visible difference to how the business operates.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: A very small, self-contained adjustment to one existing function, with no branching logic.
levels.example: Changing a default value, label, or a single existing field.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: A single, well-understood function or rule is being added or changed.
levels.example: Adding one new validation rule to an existing screen or form.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: Several related functions are affected, or a moderately branched workflow is involved.
levels.example: Adding a new approval step that touches a handful of connected screens.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Many interacting functions, complex business rules, or extensive conditional logic are involved.
levels.example: Reworking a multi-step order-processing workflow with several interdependent business rules.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: An enterprise-wide functional change spanning multiple business processes or a full workflow redesign.
levels.example: Redesigning the end-to-end quote-to-cash process across several departments.

dimensions.question: How difficult is the underlying technical implementation, independent of the business logic?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No new technical implementation is required beyond existing, unchanged code.
levels.example: A documentation-only or configuration-label change with no code path affected.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: Uses a pattern the team has implemented many times before, with no new tools or approach.
levels.example: Adding a field to a form using the exact same pattern used elsewhere in the app.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: Uses established, well-understood patterns and technology already in active use on this project.
levels.example: Reusing an existing internal service to add a similar, familiar capability.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: Involves a moderately unfamiliar technical approach or a technology the team has used only occasionally.
levels.example: Integrating a library or service the team has touched once or twice before.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Involves unproven technology for this team or a significant architectural change.
levels.example: Introducing a new communication pattern, such as asynchronous messaging, not previously used in this system.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Requires advanced, unproven technical problem-solving with no established precedent on this project.
levels.example: Building a novel technical capability with no comparable prior implementation to draw from.

dimensions.question: How much does this work depend on connecting to other systems?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No external system integration is involved at all.
levels.example: A change fully contained within one application with no outside calls.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: A single integration that is already fully proven and documented, used the same way as before.
levels.example: Reusing an existing, stable integration with no new configuration.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: One well-documented integration with a clear, known interface.
levels.example: Calling one existing, well-documented internal API.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: A small number of integrations with known interfaces.
levels.example: Connecting to two or three systems whose interfaces are already documented and understood.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Many integrations, or integrations with poorly documented interfaces.
levels.example: Coordinating data exchange with several systems, some with incomplete documentation.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Many integrations with systems outside the team's control, or interfaces that are largely undocumented.
levels.example: Integrating with multiple third-party or vendor systems whose behavior is not fully known in advance.

dimensions.question: How much data modeling, transformation, or migration is involved?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No data model or data content changes are involved.
levels.example: A change that reads existing data without altering its structure or content.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: A trivial, well-understood data change with no migration required.
levels.example: Adding a single optional field to an existing record with a safe default.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: A small, well-understood schema change or a small, bounded data migration.
levels.example: Adding a new column and backfilling it from an existing field.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: A moderate schema change or a bounded data migration affecting more than one table or entity.
levels.example: Restructuring a few related tables and migrating existing records into the new structure.

levels.label: High
levels.description: A large-scale migration or a complex transformation across multiple systems or data stores.
levels.example: Migrating a significant volume of historical data between two differently structured systems.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Large-scale migration combined with data-quality remediation or complex, multi-source transformation.
levels.example: Consolidating and cleaning data from several legacy sources into a single new data model.

dimensions.question: How much test effort and coordination does this work require?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No new testing is required beyond what already exists and is unaffected.
levels.example: A change with no functional or technical impact to verify.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: Straightforward test cases with essentially no regression surface.
levels.example: Verifying a single new field behaves as expected in isolation.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: Straightforward test cases with a small, well-understood regression surface.
levels.example: Testing one new function plus its immediate, well-known neighbors.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: A moderate regression surface, or some coordination across teams or components is needed.
levels.example: Testing a change that touches a few screens maintained by more than one team.

levels.label: High
levels.description: An extensive regression surface, complex test-data needs, or coordination across multiple systems.
levels.example: Full regression testing across a multi-step workflow with several dependent systems.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Extensive regression surface combined with complex test-data preparation and cross-system, cross-team coordination.
levels.example: End-to-end testing across several integrated systems with specially prepared test data and multiple test teams involved.

dimensions.question: How much does this work depend on other teams, vendors, or unresolved decisions?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No dependency on other teams, vendors, or pending decisions exists.
levels.example: Work that a single team can fully complete on its own.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: A dependency exists but is minor and nearly resolved, needing little active coordination.
levels.example: Waiting on a small configuration value from another team that has already committed to a delivery date.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: One or two known, manageable dependencies on other teams or vendors.
levels.example: Needing a small API change from another internal team before this work can complete.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: Several known dependencies that require active coordination and tracking.
levels.example: Coordinating delivery timing across two or three teams or vendors with different schedules.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Multiple dependencies outside the team's control, or dependencies on decisions that are not yet finalized.
levels.example: Work that cannot fully proceed until a vendor contract and an internal architecture decision are both settled.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Numerous dependencies outside the team's control combined with materially unresolved decisions.
levels.example: Delivery depends on several external vendors and on a business decision that has not yet been made.

dimensions.question: How much risk does this work introduce to production stability, security, or compliance?

levels.label: None or Not Applicable
levels.description: No production impact, sensitive data, or compliance exposure is involved.
levels.example: Work performed entirely outside any production system.

levels.label: Very Low
levels.description: Minimal, low-likelihood production impact with no sensitive data or compliance exposure.
levels.example: A change isolated to a non-critical, low-traffic internal tool.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: Minimal production impact in a component that is used but not on the critical path, with no sensitive data or compliance exposure.
levels.example: A small change to a reporting feature that does not affect core transactions.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: Some production impact, or moderate handling of sensitive data.
levels.example: A change to a customer-facing feature that handles personal contact information.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Significant production impact, sensitive-data exposure, or a compliance-relevant change.
levels.example: A change to payment processing or a system that stores regulated personal data.

levels.label: Very High
levels.description: Major production impact combined with sensitive-data exposure or direct compliance or regulatory relevance.
levels.example: A change to core financial transaction processing that is subject to regulatory audit.
